An 'Index Account' is a sub-account where interest is credited based on the measured performance of an external index.
An 'Index Account' does not involve direct ownership of any securities.
A 'Segment' is a designated allocation unit within an Index Account.
Each Segment carries its own start date.
Each Segment carries its own end date.
Each Segment carries its own crediting parameters.
For applicable accounts, the High-Water Mark is the highest index value recorded on any monthly anniversary within the crediting period.
A 'Spread' is a deduction applied to index gains prior to crediting.
A Spread may be used in lieu of or in addition to a cap rate.
For Buffer Accounts, a 'Buffer' is the percentage of index loss absorbed by the company before losses affect the account value.
The Crediting Period refers to the duration of a Segment.
The crediting period for the S&P 500 Annual Point-to-Point account is 1 year.
The Crediting Period length is specified per account.
CVAT stands for Cash Value Accumulation Test.
CVAT is the IRC §7702 tax qualification method elected for this policy.
